newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar posts $1.36 billion profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar posts $1.36 billion profit in 1996.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc. Tuesday reported record profits of $1.36 billion for 1996 on record revenues but said it expected flat results this year.
The world's largest heavy equipment maker reported that profits in the fourth quarter jumped 27 percent.
Peoria, Ill.-based Caterpillar said earnings for all of 1996 rose from 1995's $1.14 billion while revenues grew 2.8 percent to $16.52 billion from $16.07 billion.
For the fourth quarter, profits rose to $381 million, or $1.99 a share, from $300 million, or $1.53 a share in the 1995 quarter.
Caterpillar's fourth-quarter results exceeded Wall Street analysts' average estimate of $1.88 a share, according to First Call Corp., which tracks earnings estimates.
But investors pushed its stock down $1.75 to $76.75 in morning New York Stock Exchange trading, apparently on concerns about the outlook for 1997.
The company said it expected to post 1997 profits nearly flat with 1996 levels, with revenues from ongoing operations growing only slightly.
Caterpillar said higher demand in developing regions should offset a slightly weaker market for its machines in the United States and Japan this year.
It said profit margins as a percent of sales rose to 25.2 percent in 1996 from 22.3 percent in 1995 due to higher prices and the effect of the stronger dollar against the yen and European currencies.
Lower material costs and improvements in the manufacturing process also helped.
Total capital expenditures in 1996 were $642 million and are expected to increase 10 to 15 percent in 1997, Caterpillar said.

"In 1997, we plan to increase spending for capital assets, research and product development to enhance our prospects for long-term growth and profitability," Chairman Donald Fites said in a statement. "In addition, we intend to increase our investments for new business opportunities around the globe."
Major initiatives include electric power generation, agricultural products, mining systems, compact machines and strengthening the company's product support system, Caterpillar said.
Research and development spending is expected to rise 20 percent from $410 million in 1996, the company said.
